Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Apply explicit corrections to the final stated intent. Preserve meaningful filler-like words and unfinished thoughts. Apply clearly spoken punctuation and list cues. Keep the supplied language.", "input": "the seed exchange at cedar lane garden is on april twentieth in the tool shed not the greenhouse because the greenhouse is booked for the school visit we expect about thirty people and mara is bringing the folding tables i have the bean packets from last year but we need fresh labels for the runner beans and the yellow wax beans first, we should set out the sign in sheet and the small paper envelopes then put the tomato seeds on the back table so they do not get mixed with the herbs i was going to ask everyone to bring six packets no, three packets each is enough because we have fewer tables than last spring the library has offered two trays and a roll of masking tape but they have not confirmed whether someone can stay until noon please remind people that seeds should be dry and marked with the plant name and year jo said she can bring the old garden map and i will bring the jars for the beans we usually give extras to the after school club though this time we should keep one packet of each variety for the new beds if the north bed stays wet through friday, we would", "output": "The seed exchange at Cedar Lane Garden is on April 20 in the tool shed, not the greenhouse, because the greenhouse is booked for the school visit. We expect about 30 people, and Mara is bringing the folding tables. I have the bean packets from last year, but we need fresh labels for the runner beans and the yellow wax beans.

First, we should set out the sign-in sheet and the small paper envelopes. Then put the tomato seeds on the back table so they do not get mixed with the herbs. I was going to ask everyone to bring six packets—no, three packets each is enough because we have fewer tables than last spring. The library has offered two trays and a roll of masking tape, but they have not confirmed whether someone can stay until noon.

Please remind people that seeds should be dry and marked with the plant name and year. Jo said she can bring the old garden map, and I will bring the jars for the beans. We usually give extras to the after-school club, though this time we should keep one packet of each variety for the new beds. If the north bed stays wet through Friday, we would"}]
